entries.title: The harness is all you need (mostly)
entries.author: GitHub

summary.text: A simple GitHub Copilot workflow for prototyping, planning, implementing, and reviewing software without relying on new AI tools. By mastering the harness, developers can improve their effectiveness with AI. The workflow includes picking a tool, turning on YOLO mode, starting with a prototype, planning methodically, implementing with Autopilot, human review and iteration, and rubber ducking the result.
takeaways: Mastering the harness is key to improving effectiveness with AI
YOLO mode allows agents to execute commands without permission
Prototyping helps uncover nuances and avoid rework
Planning methodically with the model identifies edge cases
Autopilot implements the plan with subagents and multimodel workflows
Human review and iteration ensure quality results

entries.title: 打开 Agent Trading 的新世界大门：一步一步搭一个能自己跑的交易系统
entries.author: Balder

summary.text: 本文介绍如何构建一个自动化交易系统，通过使用 Agent Trading 来严格执行交易策略。Agent Trading 允许用户定义复杂的交易规则，并通过程序自动执行。文中提供了一个六步教程，指导用户如何配置环境、选择策略、验证系统和搭建监控面板。
takeaways: Agent Trading 可以严格执行交易策略
通过程序自动执行交易规则
需要配置环境、选择策略、验证系统和搭建监控面板
自动化交易存在重大风险，需要充分测试和谨慎使用

summary.text: Codex's Multi-Agent V2 tools enable Sol and Terra to collaborate on complex tasks, with Sol delegating tasks, sharing updates, and coordinating with other agents. This allows for more efficient and effective work. By adjusting reasoning effort and context inheritance, users can optimize agent collaboration for specific tasks.
takeaways: Sol can delegate tasks to other agents, including Terra, to complete complex tasks
Agents can inherit context from their parent or start with a fresh assignment
Users can configure concurrency, reasoning effort, and context inheritance to optimize agent collaboration
A coordinator agent can assign substantive work, track progress, and avoid duplicate investigations
Agents can message each other directly through a common messaging system

summary.text: The article discusses the limitations of software factories that rely on AI coding agents, highlighting the importance of human oversight in maintaining codebase quality. Despite the promise of increased velocity and efficiency, the author argues that models cannot maintain and improve codebase quality over time without human steering.
takeaways: Software factories that rely on AI coding agents can lead to decreased codebase quality over time.
Models cannot maintain and improve codebase quality without human steering.
Human oversight is necessary to prevent the degradation of codebase quality.
The lights-off software factory approach, where humans do not read code, is flawed.
Front-loading alignment and planning can help reduce rework and improve code quality.

entries.title: How we built our knowledge base
entries.author: Cerebras
entries.authors: Isaac Tai, Daniel Kim, Mike Gao

summary.text: Cerebras' internal knowledge base answers 15,000+ questions a day from humans, automations, and agents. The core bet: don't centralize information — pull it from where it already lives (Slack, GitHub, docs, Jira) into one Postgres embeddings table, then stack hybrid retrieval on top.
takeaways: Slack search = full-text + embeddings + IDF + recency decay, fused with RRF and a reranker; threads get LLM-distilled into a searchable question/summary/resolution.
Code repos up to 40 GB are embedded incrementally with CocoIndex — only changed chunks re-embed per commit.
Query time: an LLM planner fans tools out in parallel (search, Slack, ripgrep, recent PRs, who_knows), then fuses, reranks, and synthesizes.
Two front doors: MCP exposes raw retrieval primitives for agents; the web UI runs the full planner → executor → synthesizer pipeline for humans.
Projects scope search to teams, so compiler engineers don't drown in infra runbooks.
